next_steps: Maya to send 1-pager with joint value props and TCV estimate by 2026-07-16
Liam to run a 10k-token latency/cost micro-benchmark and share results by 2026-07-20
Schedule exec alignment (Redwood AE + Skylark VP) — propose 2026-07-23, Maya to send invite
action_items: Maya Chen | Send co-sell one-pager, joint value props, and draft partnership tranche plan | 2026-07-16
Liam Rodriguez | Run preliminary perf/latency bench on Skylark sample prompts, include KV cache behavior notes | 2026-07-20
Samir Patel | Provide top-10 pilot account list and expected go-live windows | 2026-07-18

meeting_header: Date: 2026-07-14 | Time: 15:00-15:52 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Location: Zoom | Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Liam Rodriguez (SE), Arjun Mehta (Partner GTM) | Skylark: Ethan Park, Rachel Byrne, Samir Patel, Nina Gomez
summary: Joint deal sprint to align on co-sell play, identify technical risks (latency & private data paths), and agree next steps for a pilot with Skylark's top accounts. Main blockers: Skylark needs VPC/VPN details, clear TCO math vs ApexServe, and procurement timelines for an early Q4 pilot.
questions: What SLA/latency targets do Skylark customers demand?
Do Skylark pilots require on-prem or is VPC enough?
Which accounts can we prioritize for a co-sell pilot?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone can hear me? um good afternoon, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood — i'm the AE on the partner motion. quick intros please.
[00:24] Ethan Park: Ethan here, head of cloud partnerships at Skylark. hey Maya, thanks.
[00:35] Rachel Byrne: Rachel — sales director, i'll own the motion on our side.
[00:42] Samir Patel: Samir, VP solutions engineering — i'll handle the technical bit.
[00:48] Nina Gomez: Nina, procurement, i'll jump in later.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Great. Liam from our infra team is on the line — Liam?
[00:58] Liam Rodriguez: Hey hi all, Liam Rodriguez, solutions engineer — i'll do the latency and deployment questions.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Cool, agenda: 1) quick alignment on target accounts for pilot, 2) techni — the tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated/private, 3) risk triage and benchmark plan, 4) next steps. we'll keep this tight.
[01:28] Ethan Park: Sounds good. Quick note — Skylark's top priority is low tail-latency for customer-facing flows, anything above ~350ms at 512 tokens is a concern. Cost is secondary but still material.
[01:45] Rachel Byrne: timeline: we'd like a pilot in Q4, ideally Sept-Nov window to show to two anchor accounts. procurement might push dates though.
[01:55] Maya Chen: Got it. On the pilot accounts — which two are anchor-ish?
[02:02] Samir Patel: We have AceroTech and Meridian Health as the immediate candidates. Acero's compliance bar is moderate, Meridian is strict healthcare, so they'd want data residency + audit trails.
[02:18] Maya Chen: okay good. That suggests we'll probably need options for Private/VPC or at least dedicated capacity with strong audit logs. Redwood has both Dedicated and Private — Liam can outline.
[02:31] Liam Rodriguez: Sure. Quick primer: Hosted (Redwood API) is fastest to get started but shared infra; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) can satisfy strict residency and KMS/HSM needs. For Meridian we'd likely map to Private or VPC with customer-managed KMS.
[02:55] Rachel Byrne: Meridian will require SOC2 + ISO + an audit trail. Do you have those? we need to be able to show them.
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs; we also provide audit logs and per-request metadata. we'll send the security pack after this call.
[03:16] Ethan Park: Great. On the cost side, ApexServe has quoted us a blended price that's competitive; we need a 1-pager showing Redwood's value for latency, cost, and partner enablement.
[03:28] Maya Chen: We'll put together a co-sell one-pager — joint value props, expected TCO delta versus ApexServe, and typical SLA outcomes.
[03:36] Samir Patel: Now technical: latency headroom — we run between 250–600 token convs. We need median <300ms and p95 under 600ms for typical model sizes. Do you have measured perf on common Llama-family or local opt models?
[03:53] Liam Rodriguez: We have benchmark profiles for llama-2-13b equivalents and gpt-ish open models. caveat: our numbers vary with seq len and KV cache hit rates. we'll run a micro-benchmark on Skylark prompts. can we get a sample workload?
[04:08] Samir Patel: yes i'll share a sanitized prompt set and a sample token distribution. expect an upload by end of day tomorrow.
[04:15] Maya Chen: Great — Liam will run the test and include notes about continuous batching and prefix cache assumptions.
[04:23] Ethan Park: Another risk — data flow and PII: Meridian wants to ensure data doesn't leave region X. They also ask about KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[04:34] Liam Rodriguez: For region constraints we can spin up dedicated infra in region X if allowed; for KMS we support customer KMS/HSM and key rotation — we'll include the integration doc. some of the words in the doc may read 'K V cache' in auto-transcripts, sorry.
[04:49] Rachel Byrne: (laughs) noted. On procurement — Nina, what do you need from Redwood to get a PO approved?
[04:56] Nina Gomez: We need standard SOW templates, terms, and a list of sub processors. Also the timeline: how long from contract signature to pilot standing up (approx)?
[05:06] Maya Chen: Typically for Dedicated it's ~4–6 weeks for capacity prep; Private can be longer depending on networking. For a VPC private control plane, 2–4 weeks if networking is straightforward. We'll confirm exact timelines per account after we size.
[05:19] Ethan Park: So for Acero (lower compliance) we can try Hosted or Dedicated; Meridian likely Private. Let's triage the risks and decide which to push first.
[05:30] Maya Chen: Proposal: run pilot on Acero first using Dedicated for predictable latency, run benchmarks and capture cost delta. Then parallel work on Meridian requirements for Private. Thoughts?
[05:40] Samir Patel: That seems sensible. What about co-sell motion — who is the joint exec owner for the pitch?
[05:46] Arjun Mehta: Arjun here, partner GTM — Redwood will co-sponsor with Ethan; Maya will drive the technical enablement, and we'll align on an exec intro for Meridian after we have procurement timelines.
[05:58] Ethan Park: I'll coordinate internal execs. We should also build a slide that shows caching/batch lever effects: how batching reduces per-token cost but may increase tail latency — Meridian will ask that question.
[06:12] Liam Rodriguez: Exactly. We'll include a quick chart — cost vs latency tradeoff, and a recommended config for low-latency production (small batch, KV caching enabled).
[06:22] Rachel Byrne: Competitor push — ApexServe says they have an embedded model option and are emphasizing cheaper per-token costs. How do we make the financial case?
[06:31] Maya Chen: We'll produce a TCO calc: tokens per session, expected concurrency, and include reserved capacity discounts. We'll also include value from Redwood Console — token-level cost and latency breakdowns — that customers find helpful for ops.
[06:43] Nina Gomez: Procurement question: do you require long-term commitment for discounted Dedicated pricing?
[06:49] Maya Chen: Discounts typically come with reserved monthly/annual commits. We'll show a few tiers. For pilots we often provide a short-term reserved trial.
[06:58] Samir Patel: On security: Meridian needs audit logs, SAML/SSO, and RBAC. Are these available in the Private offering?
[07:07] Liam Rodriguez: Yes — Private supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs. We'll share the security architecture diagram.
[07:16] Ethan Park: Good. One concern: the Meridian team also asked about model version pinning and rollback during rollouts. Features?
[07:24] Maya Chen: We support model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants. We'll add a short runbook to the materials.
[07:35] Rachel Byrne: For the pilot success criteria — what do we need to hit? Suggested: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 600ms, error rate < 0.1%, and measured cost per session within X% of ApexServe.
[07:48] Maya Chen: That sounds like a good starting SLO. we'll codify in the one-pager and the pilot SOW.
[07:56] Samir Patel: Any legal inhibitors — data residency, sub-processors?
[08:01] Maya Chen: We'll send the sub-processor list and SOC2 artifacts. Legal can follow up after this call.
[08:08] Ethan Park: Can we get a rough timeline for the benchmark and the slide deck?
[08:12] Maya Chen: We'll deliver the one-pager and deck by EOD 2026-07-16. Benchmarks by 2026-07-20. I'll create the calendar for the exec alignment for 2026-07-23.
[08:23] Nina Gomez: For PO timelines we'll aim to see a term sheet by late July.
[08:27] Maya Chen: Alright moving into a quick risk triage — Liam?
[08:31] Liam Rodriguez: Risk 1: latency variance under load — mitigation: run tests with realistic concurrency and KV cache warm-up. Risk 2: network egress and residency — mitigation: propose Private or region-dedicated nodes. Risk 3: procurement timeline — mitigation: draft SOW and provide short-term reserved trial to accelerate evaluation.
[08:55] Ethan Park: any red flags on integration complexity?
[08:58] Liam Rodriguez: Integration is mainly an API call and optional VPC peering/privatelink. For Meridian-like customers, we expect more network and KMS work but nothing unexpected. We'll produce a checklist.
[09:11] Samir Patel: Let's talk about the demo: can Redwood run a joint demo with Acero that mimics production concurrency?
[09:18] Maya Chen: Yes, we can do a demo and a scoped benchmark. We'll need sanitized prompts and expected concurrency numbers — Samir to send.
[09:27] Ethan Park: We'll also want a co-branded slide and case use outline to show to prospects.
[09:32] Arjun Mehta: we'll help with co-brand assets.
[09:35] Rachel Byrne: One more procurement snag - does Redwood require any specific subnet ranges or static IPs for VPC peering?
[09:42] Liam Rodriguez: We can work with standard VPC peering or privatelink; for static egress IPs we can allocate. We'll include a network requirements doc.
[09:50] Maya Chen: Okay we're at the point where we should outline immediate deliverables. I'll recap: one-pager + deck (Maya), perf bench (Liam), sanitized prompt set & pilot account list (Samir/Ethan), procurement timeline & PO requirements (Nina). Anything else?
[10:05] Ethan Park: Can we also get a draft co-sell outreach template for the account execs?
[10:10] Arjun Mehta: yes i'll draft an outreach email and attach assets.
[10:14] Rachel Byrne: Great. A few quick clarifications — on rollback behavior, does Redwood keep previous model weights for instant fallback?
[10:22] Liam Rodriguez: We support quick rollback to pinned versions; the runtime manages model variants, so fallbacks are automated when configured.
[10:30] Samir Patel: Regarding KV cache — how does cache warm-up behave for first user requests? important for p95.
[10:37] Liam Rodriguez: That is a practical concern — initial requests have higher latency until cache warms; mitigation is prefix caching and pre-warming during demos. we'll document warm-up strategies.
[10:47] Nina Gomez: For the SOW, will Redwood accept Skylark's standard flow-down terms or require modifications?
[10:53] Maya Chen: We'll have legal review the flow-downs, typically some negotiation but not unusual. We'll flag anything material early.
[11:01] Ethan Park: Any other competitive behavior we should watch? ApexServe pushes low price but less mature observability. Another vendor, DyneCloud, is pitching embedded edge inference; they might be an ask for certain accounts.
[11:15] Maya Chen: Thanks for the heads up. We'll highlight Redwood Console and rollout tools as differentiators.
[11:22] Rachel Byrne: Okay if we can get the deck and bench results on the proposed dates, we'll aim to lock the Acero pilot in early Aug and Meridian alignment late Aug for Q4 pilot.
[11:32] Maya Chen: That aligns. I'll send minutes and invite for the exec alignment. Thanks everyone.
[11:37] Ethan Park: Thanks all.
[11:40] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains a few autocaption errors (e.g., 'K V cache' for KV cache). References: shared drive link to deck: https://drive.company/skylark/redwood-co-sell-deck (placeholder), security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (placeholder).
